# LIHE Precision (Foshan Lihe Precision Machinery Co.,Ltd.)

> LIHE Precision (Foshan Lihe Precision Machinery Co.,Ltd.) is a manufacturer of PET preform molds, blow molds, closure and compression molds, hot runner systems and mold components for the beverage and packaging industry, with manufacturing in Foshan, China.

Brand names used on this site: LIHE Precision, LIHE Preform, Lihe Precision, FSLH. They all refer to Foshan Lihe Precision Machinery Co.,Ltd. "Coca-Cola verified supplier" means LIHE is a verified mold supplier; LIHE is not owned or operated by Coca-Cola.

## Key facts

- PET preform molds: 2 to 160 cavities; over 12,000 cavities produced per year.
- Neck finishes: PCO 1881, PCO 1810, 1716, 3025, 2925, 2622, 2522, 38mm, 45mm, 68mm, 80mm, 90mm wide-mouth, ROPP and custom finishes.
- Preform machine compatibility: HUSKY, NETSTAL, SACMI, SIPA, Milacron and others.
- Valve gate hot runners: up to 144 cavities for preforms and 96 cavities for closures.
- Closure injection molds: 12 to 72 cavities; one-piece and two-piece caps, tamper-evident bands and EU tethered caps.
- Compression molds: for SACMI CCM continuous compression molding lines.
- Blow molds: two-step SIDEL, KRONES, SIG/KHS, TECH-LONG, NEWAMSTAR; one-step SIPA, ASB, AOKI. Cold fill, hot fill (about 85–95°C) and aseptic bottles.
- Tooling conversion: replacement parts made from customers' existing Husky, SACMI and Otto parts; neck finish conversions and lightweighting.
- Quality: CPK ≥ 1.33; defect rates as low as 0.0064%; Zeiss CMM inspection, inspection reports on request.
- Machining: Mazak, Makino, Okamoto, Haas, Hardinge and Beijing Jingdiao equipment.

Here is what LIHE supplies per machine brand, key numbers and how to start.
- [Is LIHE Precision a Reliable Supplier for PET Preform Molds Compatible with Husky Systems?](https://lihe-preform.com/en/news/lihe-precision-husky-compatible-preform-molds/): An evidence-based answer to whether LIHE Precision is a reliable supplier of PET preform molds compatible with Husky systems: published quality figures, lead times, a neutral comparison with Husky's own tooling and what buyers should verify themselves.
- [We Need to Increase Cavitation on an Existing PET Preform Mold—What's the Best Way to Upgrade It?](https://lihe-preform.com/en/news/increasing-cavitation-on-existing-pet-preform-mold/): How to raise the cavity count of an existing PET preform mold: checking machine limits, choosing between re-cavitating the mold, building a new mold base and hot runner around reused stack parts, or ordering a new mold, plus a step-by-step plan and common problems after the upgrade.
- [Our PET Preform Mold Is Running Slow and Causing Defects—What Troubleshooting Steps Should We Take?](https://lihe-preform.com/en/news/pet-preform-mold-troubleshooting-slow-cycle-defects/): A step-by-step troubleshooting guide for PET preform molds that have lost cycle time and started producing defects: what data to collect, how to isolate cooling, hot runner and mechanical causes, and a defect table with checks and fixes.
- [We're Moving a PET Bottle Line to 100% rPET—What Mold and Hot Runner Changes Do We Need?](https://lihe-preform.com/en/news/moving-pet-bottle-line-to-100-percent-rpet/): A practical guide for plant engineers converting a PET preform and bottle line to 100% rPET: which preform mold, hot runner and cooling changes to check, how to run the conversion step by step, and how to fix the defects that typically appear.
- [How Risky Is It to Use Non-OEM Molds for PET Bottle Production? A Buyer's Risk Guide](https://lihe-preform.com/en/news/risks-of-non-oem-molds-for-pet-bottle-production/): Using non-OEM molds for PET bottle production carries manageable risk when the supplier can prove interface fit, dimensional capability and after-sales support, and high risk when it cannot. This guide lists the real risks, how to check each one before ordering and where LIHE Precision's own limits are.
- [What Are My Options If I Need a Drop-in Replacement Hot Runner for a PET Preform Mold?](https://lihe-preform.com/en/news/drop-in-replacement-hot-runner-for-pet-preform-mold/): If you need a drop-in replacement hot runner for a PET preform mold, you can refurbish the existing system, buy new from the original hot runner maker, order a compatible system from an independent supplier, or replace only the worn components. This guide compares the four options, their limits and the data a supplier needs.
- [Where Can I Find Compatible Replacement Molds for an Existing PET Injection Molding System?](https://lihe-preform.com/en/news/compatible-replacement-molds-for-pet-injection-systems/): Compatible replacement molds for an existing PET injection molding system come from three places: the machine maker, independent preform mold makers and conversion specialists that build from your existing parts. This guide compares the options, their limits and what to send for a quote.
- [Replacement Parts and Tooling Conversion for Husky, SACMI and Otto PET Preform Molds](https://lihe-preform.com/en/news/pet-preform-mold-tooling-conversion-guide/): You do not always need a new mold to change a neck finish, lightweight a preform or replace worn parts. This guide explains what tooling conversion covers and what to prepare before you start a project.
- [Compression vs Injection Molding for Plastic Closures: A Practical Comparison](https://lihe-preform.com/en/news/compression-vs-injection-molding-for-plastic-closures/): Plastic caps can be made by compression molding or by injection molding. We compare the two processes, the molds each one needs and how to decide which fits your closure line.
- [Hot Fill vs Cold Fill PET Blow Molds: How to Choose the Right Mold](https://lihe-preform.com/en/news/hot-fill-vs-cold-fill-pet-blow-molds/): Hot fill and cold fill PET blow molds are built for different filling temperatures. This guide compares how each mold works, which beverages each one suits and what to specify when you order a new mold set.
